source: Directive tables of the Bareos 25.1.2 Director as carried by odir (crates/odir/src/commands/show_items.rs) plus Onesimus extensions (crates/odir/src/config_check.rs EXTENSIONS)
description: A Job resource describes one unit of work: what to back up (FileSet) from where (Client), to where (Pool, Storage) and when (Schedule), or a restore, verify, copy, migrate, consolidate or admin job.

examples.title: A nightly backup job
examples.config:
Job {
  Name = backup-web
  Type = Backup
  Level = Incremental
  Client = web-fd
  FileSet = LinuxAll
  Schedule = WeeklyCycle
  Storage = File
  Messages = Standard
  Pool = Incremental
  Full Backup Pool = Full
  Differential Backup Pool = Differential
  Write Bootstrap = "/var/lib/bareos/%c.bsr"
}

examples.title: A job with a database dump before the backup
A restore job
examples.config:
Job {
  Name = RestoreFiles
  Type = Restore
  Client = web-fd
  FileSet = LinuxAll
  Storage = File
  Pool = Incremental
  Messages = Standard
  Where = /tmp/bareos-restores
}

directives.name: Name
directives.description: Name of the job. It appears in job lists, logs and the catalog; renaming it starts a new history, so the next Incremental becomes a Full.

examples.console: configure add job name=backup-web type=Backup messages=Standard pool=Incremental

directives.name: Description
directives.description: Free text describing the job.

examples.console: configure update job=backup-web description="Nightly backup of the web server"

directives.name: Type
directives.description: What the job does: Backup, Restore, Verify, Admin (runs only its scripts), Migrate, Copy, Consolidate (Always Incremental), or Archive. Required, directly or through JobDefs.

directives.name: Protocol
directives.description: Backup protocol: Native for the Bareos File Daemon; NDMP_BAREOS or NDMP_NATIVE for NAS filers (data stored by Bareos or by an NDMP tape server).

directives.name: Backup Format
directives.description: Format of NDMP backups (for example dump or tar, depending on the filer); Native for normal jobs.

directives.name: Level
directives.description: Default level of the job: for backups Full, Incremental, Differential or VirtualFull; for verify jobs InitCatalog, Catalog, VolumeToCatalog, DiskToCatalog or Data. A Run line of the Schedule or run level= overrides it. An Incremental or Differential without a Full before it is upgraded to Full.

directives.name: Messages
directives.description: Messages resource that decides where the job's messages go (job log in the catalog, mail, log file). Required.

directives.name: Storage
directives.description: Storage the job writes to (or reads from). Several may be listed; the first available one is used. A Storage in the Pool takes precedence over the job's.

directives.name: Pool
directives.description: Pool the job writes to. Required for backups; Full Backup Pool and the other level pools and Run line overrides can choose another one per level.

directives.name: Full Backup Pool
directives.description: Pool used when the job runs at level Full, so Fulls can have their own retention.

directives.name: Virtual Full Backup Pool
directives.description: Pool a VirtualFull is written to. It must differ from the pools it reads from unless the storage has more than one device.

directives.name: Incremental Backup Pool
directives.description: Pool used for Incremental runs.

directives.name: Differential Backup Pool
directives.description: Pool used for Differential runs.

directives.name: Next Pool
directives.description: Pool that Copy, Migrate and VirtualFull jobs write to. Overrides Next Pool of the source pool.

directives.name: Client
directives.description: Client (File Daemon) the job backs up or, for restores, restores to by default. Required for backups.

directives.name: File Set
directives.description: FileSet that says what is backed up. Changing the FileSet makes the next Incremental or Differential a Full unless Ignore FileSet Changes is set.

directives.name: Schedule
directives.description: Schedule that starts the job automatically. Without it, the job only runs when it is started by hand or by another job.

directives.name: Job To Verify
directives.description: For verify jobs: the backup job whose last run is verified (levels Catalog, VolumeToCatalog, Data).

directives.name: Catalog
directives.description: Catalog for this job, overriding that of the client.

directives.name: Job Defs
directives.description: JobDefs resource whose directives this job inherits. Directives written in the job itself win. The Onesimus GUI shows which values come from the JobDefs.

directives.name: Run
directives.description: Starts another job (or a copy of this one with other settings) when this job is started, in run command syntax, for example a second backup to another storage. It is rarely needed; Copy jobs are the usual way to a second copy.

examples.console: configure update job=backup-web run="backup-web-copy level=%l since=\"%s\""

directives.name: Where
directives.description: For restore jobs: directory prefix the files are restored under. / restores to the original place. The restore command and the GUI can change it per restore, within the console's Where ACL.

directives.name: Regex Where
directives.description: For restore jobs: rewrites the paths of restored files with sed-like expressions (!from!to!), instead of a plain prefix.

directives.name: Strip Prefix
directives.description: For restore jobs: removes this prefix from the paths before restoring.

directives.name: Add Prefix
directives.description: For restore jobs: adds this prefix to the paths (like Where).

directives.name: Add Suffix
directives.description: For restore jobs: adds this suffix to the restored file names, for example to keep existing files.

directives.name: Bootstrap
directives.description: Bootstrap file a restore job reads to find the data on the volumes. Usually written by the restore command itself.

directives.name: Write Bootstrap
directives.description: File (or, starting with |, a command) the job writes its bootstrap to after a backup: which volumes and blocks hold this job. With it a restore is possible even without the catalog, so keep it off the backup server. %c, %n and other job variables are replaced.

directives.name: Write Verify List
directives.description: Deprecated: file the verify job writes its list of files to.

directives.name: Replace
directives.description: For restore jobs: what happens to files that exist already: always (overwrite), ifnewer (only if the backup is newer), ifolder (only if it is older) or never.

directives.name: Maximum Bandwidth
directives.description: Limits the bandwidth of this job. Speeds take the suffixes k/s, m/s (powers of 1024) or kb/s, mb/s (powers of 1000); a plain number means bytes per second.

directives.name: Max Run Sched Time
directives.description: Cancels the job if it has not finished this long after its scheduled time (waiting counts). Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Max Run Time
directives.description: Cancels the job if it runs longer than this from its actual start. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Full Max Runtime
directives.description: Max Run Time for Full runs only. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Incremental Max Runtime
directives.description: Max Run Time for Incremental runs only. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Differential Max Runtime
directives.description: Max Run Time for Differential runs only. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Max Wait Time
directives.description: Cancels the job if it waits longer than this for a resource (a volume, a device, a concurrency slot) after it started. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Max Start Delay
directives.description: Cancels the job if it cannot start within this time after its scheduled time, so a nightly job that missed its window does not run in the day. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Max Full Interval
directives.description: Upgrades an Incremental or Differential to Full when the last successful Full is older than this. A simple way to get regular Fulls without a Full Run line. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Max Virtual Full Interval
directives.description: Upgrades a run to VirtualFull when the last VirtualFull (or Full) is older than this. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Max Diff Interval
directives.description: Upgrades an Incremental to Differential when the last Differential is older than this. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Prefix Links
directives.description: For restores with Where: also prefix the targets of absolute symbolic links, so they point into the restore directory.

directives.name: Prune Jobs
directives.description: Prune the job records of this job's client after the job, as if the retention had been applied by prune jobs.

directives.name: Prune Files
directives.description: Prune the file records of this job's client after the job.

directives.name: Prune Volumes
directives.description: Prune the volumes of the pool after the job.

directives.name: Purge Migration Job
directives.description: After a successful migration, purge the migrated (source) job from the catalog.

directives.name: Enabled
directives.description: A disabled job is not started by its schedule; it can still be run by hand. enable job and disable job change it at run time.

directives.name: Spool Attributes
directives.description: Spool the file attributes on the Storage Daemon and insert them into the catalog at the end of the job, instead of while writing. Speeds up jobs with many small files.

directives.name: Spool Data
directives.description: Spool the data to disk on the Storage Daemon first and write it to the volume in big chunks. Meant for tape drives that would otherwise stop and start (shoe-shining). It implies Spool Attributes.

directives.name: Spool Size
directives.description: Upper limit of the spool file of this job. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

directives.name: Rerun Failed Levels
directives.description: If the last Full (or Differential) failed, run the next job at that level again instead of the scheduled lower level.

directives.name: Prefer Mounted Volumes
directives.description: Prefer a drive that has a usable volume mounted. With no, the Director prefers an idle drive, which spreads jobs over several drives.

directives.name: Run Before Job
directives.description: Command the Director runs before the job; a failing command cancels the job. Short form of a RunScript with RunsWhen = Before on the Director.

directives.name: Run After Job
directives.description: Command the Director runs after a successful job (RunScript, RunsWhen = After, RunsOnFailure = no).

directives.name: Run After Failed Job
directives.description: Command the Director runs after a failed job.

directives.name: Client Run Before Job
directives.description: Command the File Daemon runs on the client before the backup, for example a database dump. A failing command cancels the job.

directives.name: Client Run After Job
directives.description: Command the File Daemon runs on the client after the job.

directives.name: Maximum Concurrent Jobs
directives.description: How many runs of this job may run at the same time; usually 1, so a slow run is not overtaken by the next one.

directives.name: Reschedule On Error
directives.description: Start the job again when it failed, after Reschedule Interval, at most Reschedule Times times.

directives.name: Reschedule Interval
directives.description: Wait between a failed run and its retry. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Reschedule Times
directives.description: How many times a failed job is retried; 0 means without limit.

directives.name: Priority
directives.description: Priority of the job: smaller numbers first. Jobs of different priorities do not run at the same time (unless Allow Mixed Priority): a job waits until all jobs of a higher priority are done. Use it for example to run the catalog backup after all others. The schedule view of the Onesimus GUI does not count such waits as avoidable.

directives.name: Allow Mixed Priority
directives.description: Allow this job to run together with jobs of other priorities, as long as they allow it as well.

directives.name: Selection Pattern
directives.description: For Copy and Migrate jobs: the pattern or SQL query used by Selection Type (a job or client name pattern, or a query returning job IDs).

directives.name: Run Script
directives.description: Block that runs a command or console command before or after the job, on the Director or the client, with control over failure handling. See the RunScript block.

directives.name: Selection Type
directives.description: For Copy and Migrate jobs: how the source jobs are chosen: SmallestVolume, OldestVolume, Client, Volume, Job, SQLQuery, PoolOccupancy, PoolTime, PoolUncopiedJobs.

directives.name: Accurate
directives.description: Accurate mode: the File Daemon receives the file list of the previous backups and also records deleted and renamed files, so a restore gives exactly the state of the backup. Needed for Always Incremental and VirtualFull; costs memory on the client.

directives.name: Allow Duplicate Jobs
directives.description: Allow a second run of the same job while one is queued or running. With no, the Cancel ... Duplicates directives decide which one is canceled.

directives.name: Allow Higher Duplicates
directives.description: Deprecated: allow duplicates of a higher level.

directives.name: Cancel Lower Level Duplicates
directives.description: With Allow Duplicate Jobs = no: cancel the duplicate of the lower level (an Incremental gives way to a Full).

directives.name: Cancel Queued Duplicates
directives.description: With Allow Duplicate Jobs = no: cancel a duplicate that is still waiting in the queue.

directives.name: Cancel Running Duplicates
directives.description: With Allow Duplicate Jobs = no: cancel the duplicate that is already running in favour of the new one.

directives.name: Save File History
directives.description: For NDMP: store the file history sent by the filer, so single files can be restored.

directives.name: File History Size
directives.description: For NDMP: size of the file history buffer. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

directives.name: FD Plugin Options
directives.description: Options passed to the File Daemon plugins of this job.

directives.name: SD Plugin Options
directives.description: Options passed to the Storage Daemon plugins of this job.

directives.name: Dir Plugin Options
directives.description: Options passed to the Director plugins of this job.

directives.name: Max Concurrent Copies
directives.description: For Copy jobs: how many copy jobs are started at once from one selection.

directives.name: Always Incremental
directives.description: Always Incremental scheme: only Incrementals are taken, and a Consolidate job merges the old ones into a VirtualFull. Needs Accurate and pools for the consolidated data.

directives.name: Always Incremental Job Retention
directives.description: Incrementals younger than this are not consolidated. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Always Incremental Keep Number
directives.description: How many Incrementals are always kept unconsolidated, even when they are older than the retention.

directives.name: Always Incremental Max Full Age
directives.description: When the Full of an Always Incremental chain is older than this, the Consolidate job includes it, so the Full does not grow old. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

directives.name: Max Full Consolidations
directives.description: How many Fulls a Consolidate job may consolidate in one run (because of Always Incremental Max Full Age); 0 means no limit. Only valid for Consolidate jobs.

directives.name: Run On Incoming Connect Interval
directives.description: For clients that connect to the Director (Connection From Client To Director): start this job when the client connects and the last run is older than this interval. 0 switches it off. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

blocks.name: RunScript
blocks.description: Runs a command or console command before or after the job, on the Director or the client. Several RunScript blocks may be given.

directives.name: Command
directives.description: Shell command to run; repeatable. Job variables are replaced: %c client, %d Director, %e exit status, %i JobId, %j unique job name, %l level, %n job name, %s since time, %t job type, %v volume names.

examples.config: Command = "/usr/local/bin/dump-database %l"

directives.name: Console
directives.description: Console command the Director runs instead of a shell command, for example to start another job or update a volume.

examples.config: Console = "update stats days=30"

directives.name: Runs When
directives.description: When the script runs: Before the job, After it, AfterVSS (Windows, after the snapshot), Always (before and after) or Queued (when the job enters the queue).

examples.config: Runs When = Before

directives.name: Runs On Client
directives.description: Run the command on the client (by the File Daemon) instead of on the Director.

examples.config: Runs On Client = no

directives.name: Runs On Success
directives.description: Run the script after a successful job.

examples.config: Runs On Success = yes

directives.name: Runs On Failure
directives.description: Run the script after a failed job as well, for example to clean up.

examples.config: Runs On Failure = yes

directives.name: Fail Job On Error
directives.description: A script that exits with an error fails the job (for Before scripts: the job does not run).

examples.config: Fail Job On Error = no
